sections.title: Japan Joins U.S. Genesis Mission as First International Partner in $1 Billion AI Science Initiative
sections.body: The U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) and Japan's 文部科学省 (MEXT, Monbu Kagakusho) and 経済産業省 (METI, Keizai Sangyosho) announced on June 4-5 that Japan will become the first international partner in the DOE's Genesis Mission — a national initiative aimed at doubling American research productivity within a decade by deploying 人工知能 (jinko chino, artificial intelligence) across critical scientific domains. The arrangement commits $500 million from each nation over five years, for a combined $1 billion. The partnership will connect 12 U.S. DOE national laboratories with 12 Japanese research institutions, with priority focus on 量子技術 (ryoshi gijutsu, quantum technology) , 核融合 (kaku yugo, nuclear fusion) , biotechnology, materials science, and advanced manufacturing AI. The decision to frame Japan as a "first international partner" — ahead of European allies with longer-standing science collaboration treaties — carries deliberate strategic weight. METI's formal involvement signals Japan is treating this as industrial policy, not academic exchange. The Genesis Mission's focus areas map closely onto Japan's domestic priorities: materials science connects to semiconductor substrate supply chains; quantum technology overlaps with the Quantum Technology Innovation Program ( 量子イノベーション推進戦略 ) launched in 2020; fusion research links to the ITER project and domestic compact reactor development at 京都大学 (Kyoto Daigaku, Kyoto University) . The 12 Japanese partner institutions have not been formally named, but RIKEN ( 理化学研究所 , Japan's leading national research institute) and the National Institutes for Natural Sciences are the most likely anchors. For investors focused on Japan's research-to-commercialisation pipeline, the Genesis Mission partnership creates a formal conduit between U.S. computing infrastructure — DOE labs hold some of the world's most powerful supercomputing clusters — and Japan's precision manufacturing base. NTT Research, which already maintains a U.S. presence in quantum and photonics, is positioned to interface with this program. The $500 million Japanese commitment is modest relative to METI's ¥387.3 billion ($2.4B) domestic AI budget, suggesting Genesis Mission serves more as a strategic alignment signal than a primary funding lever. The clearest near-term watch will be whether RIKEN and partner institutions receive earmarked compute allocation from U.S. facilities under the five-year plan, and whether that accelerates publication output in fusion and materials science with domestic commercial read-through.
sections.source: Japan Times · Nippon.com · HPCwire · FedScoop · June 5, 2026

sections.title: Rapidus Completes 150 Billion Yen Government Capital Round, Bringing Total Funding to 424.95 Billion Yen
sections.body: ラピダス (Rapidus) announced on June 5 the completion of an additional funding round of ¥150 billion (approximately $943 million) from the 情報処理推進機構 (IPA, Joho Shori Suishin Kiko) — an independent administrative agency under METI's jurisdiction that serves as the government's primary vehicle for direct equity-equivalent capitalization of strategic technology companies. The latest round brings cumulative IPA contributions to ¥274.95 billion, and the company's total funding across all sources — public and private — to ¥424.95 billion. Earlier this year, Rapidus secured a ¥267.6 billion combined round involving 32 private-sector co-investors including Canon, the Development Bank of Japan, Fujitsu ( 富士通 ), NTT, SoftBank ( ソフトバンク ), and Sony Group ( ソニーグループ ). The company's stated objective remains the launch of full-scale 2-nanometer ( 2ナノメートル ) logic 半導体 (handotai, semiconductor) production by 2027 at the IIM-1 fab in 千歳 (Chitose, Hokkaido) . The funding structure warrants close reading. IPA rounds are direct government capitalization through a state-owned intermediary — structurally more like equity injection than grant subsidy, meaning they strengthen Rapidus's balance sheet and reduce near-term dilution risk from external debt. The ¥150 billion addition is the third IPA capital increase, consistent with a government commitment to provide runway in stages rather than a single lump sum, preserving leverage over project milestones. The private ¥167.6 billion from 32 companies provides co-investment optics, though the investor list is composed entirely of major keiretsu members, which means the private capital is partly strategic. Total government-equivalent funding now exceeds ¥424 billion, though estimates of the full government commitment including METI subsidies, tax credits, and IPA capitalization are substantially higher — industry analysts have cited figures approaching ¥2.35 trillion in cumulative support commitments across all instruments. The critical variable that no funding round resolves is external customer commitment. IBM has provided EUV process technology under a 2023 partnership and remains the most prominent potential anchor customer for Rapidus's 2nm node, but no supply agreement has been publicly disclosed. The business model requires Rapidus to attract high-volume logic customers — likely hyperscalers, automotive AI chip designers, or sovereign AI programs — who will commit wafer starts two to three years in advance. Without that, the company's ¥424.95 billion in funding is seed capital for an industry-scale bet that depends on demand that does not yet have a name attached to it. For semiconductor equipment investors, the ongoing Rapidus funding trajectory keeps Tokyo Electron's domestic order pipeline visible for 2027; the more important data point will be TEL's July earnings, where management may comment on Rapidus equipment delivery schedules.
sections.source: PR Newswire · MLex · Digital Watch Observatory · June 5, 2026

sections.title: Japan's May Reserves Fall by Record Amount as MOF Renews Yen Defense Pledge Near 160
sections.body: Japan's 財務省 (Ministry of Finance, MOF) released May foreign exchange reserve data on June 5, confirming a record drop in 外貨準備 (gaika junbi, foreign currency reserves) consistent with the largest 為替介入 (kawase kainyū, currency intervention) program in Japan's history. Between April 28 and May 27, authorities deployed approximately ¥11.73 trillion ($73.6 billion) in yen-buying operations, triggered initially after USD/JPY breached the politically significant 160 level. The drawdown brought reserves to their lowest level in several years. Simultaneously, Finance Minister 片山さつき (Katayama Satsuki) reiterated on June 5 that Japan will take "decisive action" against excessively volatile FX moves at any time, and confirmed authorities remain in close contact with U.S. officials on currency matters — a phrasing that has historically preceded coordinated G7 intervention discussions. The yen was trading at approximately 159.9 per dollar on Friday, a third consecutive session probing the 160 level. The release crystallizes the intervention arithmetic clearly. Goldman Sachs estimated in early May that Japan held sufficient reserves for approximately 30 more interventions at the scale of the April-May program. The record May drawdown narrows that buffer, but Japan's remaining reserve base — still above $1 trillion — means the MOF retains considerable capacity. The more substantive constraint is political: the April-May intervention was the first since July 2024, and repeat operations risk U.S. Treasury pushback, particularly given language in the most recent U.S. Foreign Exchange Report. Prime Minister 高市早苗 (Takaichi Sanae) framed sustainable yen strength as requiring economic fundamentals improvement, which implicitly acknowledges the limits of intervention as a standalone tool. The structural driver of yen weakness — a roughly 300 basis point gap between the BOJ's policy rate (0.75%) and U.S. Federal Funds rate (3.50-3.75%) — remains intact. The June 16 BOJ meeting, where markets are pricing approximately 80% probability of a 25bp hike to 1.00%, is the next potential inflection point. However, a single 25bp BOJ move will not close the rate gap enough to materially shift the carry trade calculus; the yen may only begin a durable recovery if the BOJ's post-meeting guidance signals that the pace of further hikes will accelerate beyond what markets currently price. For Japan equity investors, the yen near 160 creates divergent sector outcomes: domestic demand stocks and import-price-sensitive consumer companies are insulated or benefit from reflation; export manufacturers face translation headwinds on repatriated earnings if the yen continues to weaken from here.
sections.source: InvestingLive · Reuters · Bloomberg · June 5, 2026

title: Japan AI Index Launches · Kioxia First Dividend · BOJ Two-Hike Path
audio_label: Japan AI Index · Kioxia Dividend and Semi Rally
summary: The University of Tokyo, Anthropic, and PKSHA Technology launched the Japan AI Index on June 4, the first academic framework to measure generative AI adoption across Japan using real usage data. Separately, Kioxia Holdings announced its first-ever dividend backed by AI-driven NAND demand, driving the Nikkei to a record 68,402, while Bloomberg reported BOJ officials are considering not just a June hike to 1% but an additional rise later in 2026.

sections.title: Tokyo University, Anthropic, and PKSHA Launch Japan's First Generative AI Adoption Index
sections.body:
On June 4, the Matsuo-Iwasawa Lab at the University of Tokyo, AI software company PKSHA Technology, and Anthropic announced the creation of the Japan AI Index — the first framework in Japan designed to produce a systematic, evidence-based measurement of how generative AI (生成AI, seisē AI) is reshaping employment, industries, productivity, and education across the country. The partnership marks Anthropic's first full-scale collaboration with a Japanese academic institution.

The methodology is notably different from conventional AI adoption surveys, which rely on self-reported company data and are prone to selection bias. The Japan AI Index will cross-reference anonymised usage data from Anthropic's Claude with official Japanese government statistics — output and employment data from the Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications, and economic accounts from the Cabinet Office. The first published report is expected between October and November 2026.

For investors tracking Japan's AI productivity story, the index creates a reference data series that can anchor forward earnings expectations for Japanese enterprise software firms and AI integrators. The institutional structure — anchored at a prestigious national university with government statistical input — creates durable credibility that a purely corporate-sponsored survey would not have. Whether the October report shows meaningful penetration beyond the early-adopter technology sector will be the first real test of whether Japan's AI transition is broadening.
sections.takeaway: The Japan AI Index creates, for the first time, a credible measurement baseline for Japan's generative AI adoption — its October debut will be a key data point for investors modelling the productivity upside of Japan's AI cycle.

sections.title: Kioxia Announces First-Ever Dividend as NAND Flash Demand Drives Shares Through 80,000 Yen
sections.body:
Kioxia Holdings (キオクシア), the world's second-largest NAND flash memory maker, announced on June 3 that it intends to begin dividend payments from fiscal year 2027, citing solid earnings driven by sustained demand from AI data centre storage buildout. Kioxia shares rose 7.2 percent on the announcement, crossing the 80,000-yen level for the first time. The move helped push the Nikkei 225 to a record close of 68,402.13 — the first time the index has closed above 68,000 points. Tokyo Electron (東京エレクトロン) also rose 13.4 percent to an all-time high, contributing the largest single stock gain to the index.

Kioxia's dividend announcement is structurally significant beyond a one-day stock move. The company has been in balance-sheet repair mode since its leveraged buyout by Bain Capital in 2018 and a subsequent capital markets journey that included a failed IPO attempt before a successful listing in late 2024. A commitment to dividend payments signals that management believes the AI-driven demand for NAND flash storage — in training data lakes, inference clusters, and high-bandwidth memory adjacent applications — is durable enough to support capital returns.

The adjacent moves in Tokyo Electron (+13.4%) and Advantest (アドバンテスト, +5.1%) reinforce this read. TEL supplies wafer coating and cleaning equipment central to advanced NAND production; Advantest provides chip testing systems whose revenue scales with wafer starts. The cluster of simultaneous all-time highs across memory producer, equipment supplier, and test vendor consistently signals that investors are pricing a structural rather than cyclical shift in flash memory demand.
sections.takeaway: Kioxia's first dividend is a corporate posture shift — from balance-sheet repair to shareholder return — that prices in NAND demand durability; the adjacent moves in TEL and Advantest confirm the AI storage supply chain read-through.

sections.title: BOJ Officials Said to Be Considering June Hike to 1% and Another Rise Later in 2026
sections.body:
Bloomberg reported June 4 that the Bank of Japan (日本銀行, Nihon Ginkō) officials are prepared to consider a 25-basis-point increase in the policy rate (政策金利, seisaku kinri) at the Monetary Policy Meeting concluding June 16, which would bring the overnight rate from 0.75% to 1.00%. The report adds a detail absent from prior coverage: officials also see scope for at least one additional hike in the second half of 2026, with real interest rates still deeply negative even at 1.00% relative to current inflation. The insider framing represents a notable escalation from Governor Ueda Kazuo (植田和男)'s last public speech on June 3, which signalled the need to continue raising rates without specifying the beyond-June path.

Markets had already priced approximately 80 percent probability of a June hike; the marginal information is now a second hike within the calendar year, most likely at the September or October meeting. The June 16 press conference language will be the key test: if Ueda weakens the standard conditionality clause — in accordance with economic, price, and financial developments — or signals that the pace of accommodation removal is accelerating, that is the forward guidance that reprices the September probability from the current low teens toward 40-50 percent.

For equity positioning, the two-hike 2026 scenario creates meaningful divergence between sector exposures. Domestic banks (メガバンク, megabanku) benefit materially from a steeper JGB yield curve. Export-oriented manufacturers face a modest headwind from yen appreciation. J-REITs (不動産投資信託, fudōsan tōshi shintaku) face the most direct pressure as refinancing costs rise against fixed-income alternatives. Whether the BOJ accompanies any June hike with a revised JGB purchase tapering schedule will be the second key variable.
sections.takeaway: The 'another possible in 2026' framing from Bloomberg shifts the BOJ narrative from a one-and-done June hike to a multi-hike path — watch Ueda's conditionality language on June 16 to determine whether the September probability meaningfully reprices.

title: MHI + Preferred Networks AI Alliance · Chip Capex Watch · Ueda's Pre-Blackout Signal
audio_label: MHI + Preferred Networks Alliance · Japan Chip Capex Watch
summary: Mitsubishi Heavy Industries and Preferred Networks formalised a business alliance to build domestic AI for mission-critical infrastructure and national security, targeting a capital stake within FY2026. BOJ Governor Ueda delivered his final pre-blackout remarks on June 3, framing upside price risks as now 'greater overall and emerging sooner' — a harder lean than April's symmetric language ahead of the June 15-16 meeting.

sections.title: Mitsubishi Heavy and Preferred Networks Form AI Alliance for Mission-Critical Infrastructure
sections.body:
Mitsubishi Heavy Industries (MHI) and Preferred Networks (PFN) announced a formal business alliance on June 2, 2026, aimed at developing AI systems for Japan's social infrastructure and national security sectors. The alliance pairs MHI's decades of domain knowledge in aerospace, defense, and heavy machinery with PFN's vertically integrated AI stack — the PLaMo foundation model series, the proprietary MN-Core AI processor, and the PFCP cloud computing platform. Both companies said they intend to move toward a capital alliance within fiscal 2026.

The specific use cases framed in the announcement are autonomous situational assessment in mission-critical machinery, predictive maintenance, and rapid crisis response in high-reliability environments — systems that must operate at aerospace and defense tolerances. The emphasis on Japan-made AI throughout the press release reflects the dual influence of keizai anzenhoshō (economic security) policy and genuine preference among defense customers for domestic supply chains.

For institutional investors tracking Japan's physical AI theme, this is the most concrete example yet of a tier-one defense and energy company formalising a capital-level relationship with Japan's leading AI chipmaker. Whether the capital stake materialises on MHI's balance sheet before March 2027 is the next checkpoint.
sections.takeaway: MHI + PFN marks the first formal defense-grade AI partnership in Japan — watch MHI Q2 IR commentary for any disclosure of stake size and scope.

sections.title: Japan Chip Capex Watch: Three Milestones to Track Before the BOJ Meets on June 16
sections.body:
No single semiconductor company announcement broke in the past 48 hours, but three events are converging ahead of the BOJ June 15-16 meeting worth holding together. First, Rapidus is in the midst of its fiscal 2026 front-end wafer processing ramp at the IIM-1 facility in Chitose, Hokkaido — the transition from prototype pilot line to mass production readiness. There has been no public update from Rapidus management on yield progress since the government's April funding top-up of 631.5 billion yen, which brought total state support to 2.35 trillion yen.

Second, Micron Technology's 1.5 trillion yen ($9.6 billion) HBM facility in Hiroshima began construction in May 2026. The facility is the first dedicated high-bandwidth memory plant on Japanese soil and relies on 500 billion yen in METI subsidies. Tokyo Electron is the primary equipment supplier — its Q2 earnings in July will proxy construction pace.

Third, the yen. All of the above capex is denominated in yen against USD-priced equipment and materials. A BOJ hike on June 16 would be modestly yen-supportive, but the more important variable is guidance tone: a hawkish Ueda press conference that pushes expectations toward a second hike in September would have cleaner capex implications than the hike itself.
sections.takeaway: Watch TEL order book disclosures in July earnings as the best proxy for Japan chip capex pace — that, plus Ueda's post-June 16 guidance language, frames the second half semiconductor capex backdrop.

sections.title: Ueda's Final Pre-Blackout Remarks Signal Rate Path Intact, Upside Price Risks Now Dominant
sections.body:
BOJ Governor Ueda Kazuo said on June 3 — what appears to be his last scheduled public appearance before the pre-meeting silence period — that the Bank 'needs to keep raising rates' and, if the economy evolves in line with the Bank's outlook, it will 'continue to raise the policy interest rate at an appropriate pace.' The June 15-16 meeting is now twelve days away, with the policy rate at 0.75%.

The notable shift in Ueda's June 3 language was the assessment of balance of risks: 'upside risks to prices appear to be greater overall and are likely to emerge sooner.' That is a harder statement than the symmetric risk language the Bank has used in recent months. In the April 28 outlook report, the BOJ raised its core CPI forecast to 2.8% for fiscal 2026 while cutting growth to 0.5% — a stagflationary mix driven in part by oil prices linked to the Iran conflict and persistent pass-through from yen weakness near 160.

For positioning, the hike itself is consensus. The variable is the pace signal in the post-meeting press conference. Watch for Ueda's description of the 'degree of monetary accommodation' and whether he retains 'in accordance with economic, price, and financial developments' language from the April statement unchanged — any weakening of that conditionality would be read as a lean toward a faster pace.
sections.takeaway: The hike is priced — Ueda's press conference language on whether he retains April's conditionality wording or weakens it is the market-moving variable on June 16.

title: SoftBank #1 by Market Cap · AI Foundation Model Consortium Closes · BOJ 77% June Hike
summary: SoftBank surpassed Toyota to become Japan's most valuable company at ¥47.2T market cap (+73% YTD), simultaneously launching a sovereign AI cloud platform for government and regulated financial clients. Japan's AI Foundation Model Development Co. closes its first capital round this week with ~30 firms including Honda, Nippon Steel, MUFG, and Mizuho. OIS pricing has June 16 BOJ hike probability at 77%, but April's 6–3 vote split introduces a hold scenario the market may be underpricing.

sections.title: SoftBank Dethrones Toyota — Japan's AI Premium Reaches ¥47.2 Trillion as Sovereign Cloud Platform Launches
sections.source: Nikkei Asia · Bloomberg · AI & Equity · June 1–2, 2026
sections.body:
SoftBank Group surpassed Toyota Motor to become Japan's most valuable listed company, with a market capitalization of ¥47.2 trillion — up 73% year-to-date against Toyota's ¥40.8 trillion. ARM Holdings (~90% SoftBank-owned) accounts for ~60% of net asset value — the primary driver of the re-rating. Alongside the valuation milestone, SoftBank launched its sovereign AI cloud platform — dedicated GPU compute for Japanese government ministries and regulated financial institutions requiring domestic data residency, running on NVIDIA H100 clusters in Tokyo and Osaka.

For bulls, the sovereign cloud provides durable contracted revenue outside Vision Fund mark-to-market volatility. For bears, ¥47.2T prices in near-perfect execution on both ARM's data-centre cycle and the domestic cloud ramp. Watch Q1 FY2026 earnings (due late July) for the first sovereign cloud revenue line.
sections.takeaway: SoftBank's #1 ranking signals AI premium has definitively displaced industrial archetype in Japanese equity markets; sovereign cloud launch de-risks the thesis if government contract revenue materialises.

sections.title: Japan AI Foundation Model Consortium Closes First Capital Round — Honda, Nippon Steel, MUFG, Mizuho Among 30 Committed Investors
sections.source: Nikkei (日経新聞) · METI Press Release · Industrial Policy · June 1–2, 2026
sections.body:
Japan's AI Foundation Model Development Co. — led by SoftBank and backed by ¥1 trillion in NEDO funding — is closing its first capital tranche this week. Approximately 30 firms have formally committed, including Honda Motor (本田技研工業), Nippon Steel (日本製鉄), MUFG Bank (三菱UFJ銀行), and Mizuho Financial Group (みずほフィナンシャルグループ). The breadth (automotive, heavy industry, banking) signals national AI infrastructure with cross-sectoral governance, not a pure technology venture.

The foundation model targets trillion-parameter scale with physical-world grounding (物理AI — sensor, robotics, manufacturing data). METI has designated the entity as national infrastructure, providing preferential procurement and export-control carve-outs for compute hardware. NEDO grant is not equity — members contribute capital for preferential model-access rights.
sections.takeaway: Capital-round close this week is the first hard commitment milestone for Japan's domestically built physical AI effort — watch for secondary automotive announcements as signal of industrial co-ordination.

sections.title: June 16 BOJ Hike Probability Hits 77% — But April's 6–3 Vote Split Introduces a Hold Scenario the Market Is Underpricing
sections.source: Bloomberg · Reuters · OIS Pricing · Macro / BOJ · June 1–2, 2026
sections.body:
OIS pricing places a 77% probability on a 25bp hike at the BOJ June 15–16 Monetary Policy Meeting — highest since March 2024 negative-rate exit. Core CPI 2.8%, shuntō (春闘) wage rounds at 5%+, and the Finance Ministry's FX intervention warning all provide cover to move. A hike to 1.00% would be the fourth tightening move since March 2024 and Japan's highest nominal rate since 2008.

The April MPM vote record shows a 6–3 split with three members favouring an immediate hike — confirms hawkish direction but means downside data surprises could flip the outcome. JPMorgan base case: 'hawkish rates / dovish duration' (hike + maintained JGB purchases) settles USD/JPY at 155–157, not the 148–150 implied by pure rate-hike positioning. The statement matters more than the rate move.
sections.takeaway: 77% probability is consensus — the trade is in the statement, not the rate move; 'hawkish rates / dovish duration' is the scenario most likely to wrong-foot yen-strengthening positioning.

title: Fujitsu Dual-Frontier AI · UBS Initiates Kioxia Buy · Yen Tests 160 as June BOJ Hike Looms
summary: Fujitsu announces simultaneous AI partnerships with OpenAI and Anthropic, positioning Japan's largest IT integrator as a sovereign AI infrastructure provider. UBS initiates Kioxia with a Buy and ¥79,000 target, flagging a structural cost-per-wafer advantage. Japan's Finance Minister issues an explicit FX intervention warning as USD/JPY holds at 159.3, with a former BOJ board member calling a June rate hike 'probable'.

sections.title: Fujitsu Moves to Dual-Frontier AI — OpenAI and Anthropic Partnerships Signal a Sovereign AI Pivot
sections.source: Fujitsu Global Press Release · PR Newswire · AI & Tech · May 27, 2026
sections.body:
Fujitsu (富士通) announced simultaneous strategic partnerships with OpenAI and Anthropic on May 27, positioning Japan's largest domestic IT integrator as a dual-provider sovereign AI infrastructure player. Fujitsu Group employees will deploy ChatGPT Enterprise and Codex at scale, while the Anthropic arrangement brings Claude into government and enterprise system integration workflows — the latter sensitive for a company managing data infrastructure for Japanese government ministries.

METI has been pressing Japan's major corporates to consolidate AI adoption under domestically accountable arrangements since the AI Promotion Act. A dual-provider structure lets Fujitsu compete on enterprise bids requiring demonstrable model diversity and risk management. Both partnerships are resale-plus-integration arrangements — Fujitsu captures consulting and implementation margin. For the week ahead, watch whether any of the ~30 companies considering investment in SoftBank's Japan AI Foundation Model Development entity formally commit — approximately 10 are expected to sign in June.
sections.takeaway: Fujitsu's dual-provider move satisfies METI's sovereignty requirements while capturing implementation margin — watch June's SoftBank AI JV investor closings as the next physical AI signal.

sections.title: UBS Initiates Kioxia with Buy, Flags Structural Cost Advantage — But Cautions the Edge Narrows After BiCS10
sections.source: UBS Research · Semiconductors · May 29, 2026
sections.body:
A UBS analyst note initiating Kioxia (キオクシア) with a Buy and a ¥79,000 target found Kioxia's cost per wafer runs at approximately $2,000, against ~$4,000 for Samsung and ~$6,000 for Micron and SK Hynix. That structural advantage is rooted in Kioxia's lateral-scaling architecture and the operational leverage of its Yokkaichi and Kitakami (北上) facilities. The company's entire 2026 NAND output is already sold out. Q2 operating profit projected at ¥1.3 trillion — above its full-year FY2025 record.

UBS explicitly underwrites the cost edge through 2026–2027 then turns 'explicitly cautious' beyond that. Once Kioxia moves to BiCS10 (332-layer) and subsequent 400-plus layer generations, the throughput-per-dollar math equalizes. The implication: a 12-to-18-month trade window. The week ahead: VLSI Symposium (June 14) where Kioxia and SanDisk present their MSA-CBA 1,000-layer NAND demonstration, and NEDO expected to release updated FY2026 allocations for Rapidus (ラピダス) 2nm.
sections.takeaway: Kioxia's cost advantage is real but time-limited — UBS's 12-to-18-month window aligns with a squeeze before BiCS10 stacking equalizes with peers; VLSI June 14 is the next roadmap credibility check.

sections.title: Yen Tests 160, Finance Minister Issues Intervention Warning — Former BOJ Board Member Says June Rate Hike 'Probable'
sections.source: Japan Times · Bloomberg · CNBC · Macro / BOJ · May 30, 2026
sections.body:
Japan's Finance Minister issued an explicit FX warning on May 30, stating authorities stand ready to 'take decisive action' against excessive yen volatility after the yen (円) held at 159.3 to the dollar — near the 160 level that triggered Tokyo's first yen-buying intervention since July 2024. Former BOJ (日本銀行) board member Makoto Sakurai told Bloomberg that the BOJ will 'probably raise rates' at its June 15–16 Monetary Policy Meeting, calling it one of 'grave importance'.

The BOJ's policy rate sits at 0.75% against a US Federal Funds rate of 3.50–3.75% — a 300bp gap driving structural yen carry trade flows. The April Outlook Report cut FY2026 growth to 0.5% from 1.0% and raised core CPI to 2.8% from 1.9%. The scenario that warrants most attention: the BOJ hikes but signals extended JGB purchase commitments — 'hawkish rates / dovish duration' — which would keep yen under pressure even after a rate adjustment.
sections.takeaway: The Finance Minister's intervention warning and a former board member's June hike call both point toward BOJ action on June 15–16 — but 'hawkish rates / dovish duration' is the scenario most likely to wrong-foot yen-strengthening positioning.

title: SoftBank Dethrones Toyota · Japan Joins Genesis Mission · BOJ June 16 Hike at 80%
audio_label: SoftBank Dethrones Toyota · Japan Joins Genesis Mission
summary: SoftBank surpassed Toyota as Japan's most valuable listed company on a 75B EUR AI pledge, while Japan became the first foreign partner in the US Genesis Mission AI science programme anchored by RIKEN Fugaku. BOJ markets price an 80% probability of a June 16 rate hike with the yen near 160.

sections.title: SoftBank Dethrones Toyota as Japan's Most Valuable Company
sections.body:
SoftBank Group surpassed Toyota Motor in market capitalisation on June 1, closing at approximately 47.2 trillion yen to become Japan's highest-valued listed company. The milestone coincided with the Nikkei 225 touching 67,231 — a record — even as the TOPIX slipped 0.4%, underscoring how narrowly the AI premium is distributed within Japanese equities. SoftBank's 73% year-to-date gain reflects its 75 billion EUR commitment to AI infrastructure through its Vision Fund vehicle.

The rotation from Toyota to SoftBank marks a structural pivot in how markets are pricing the AI transition. The TOPIX underperformance on the same day SoftBank peaked signals that broader Japan equity positioning remains weighted toward cyclicals — the AI re-rating is so far a single-name story. Watch whether flows broaden to NEC, Fujitsu, and NTT Data or remain concentrated in SoftBank.
sections.takeaway: The SoftBank premium is an AI optionality bet — watch whether institutional flows rotate into other AI-adjacent Japanese names.
sections.source: Nikkei Asia · AI & Markets · June 1, 2026

sections.title: Japan Signs On as First Foreign Partner in US Genesis Mission
sections.body:
Japan formally joined the United States Genesis Mission as its first non-American partner, committing a combined $500M-$1B in AI research infrastructure. MEXT and METI officials were in Washington this week to finalise the framework. At the core of Japan's contribution is RIKEN and its Fugaku supercomputer, which provides HPC capacity to the joint programme.

The partnership validates Japan's position as a tier-one AI science partner. The dual MEXT-METI structure signals multi-year budget commitment. Fugaku joining a US-anchored AI research alliance effectively internationalises Japan's HPC asset base and could accelerate joint commercialisation with US AI labs.
sections.takeaway: RIKEN Fugaku joining Genesis Mission supports sustained government-backed demand for Japan's HPC and semiconductor equipment ecosystem.
sections.source: Japan Times · Industrial Policy · June 1, 2026

sections.title: BOJ June 16 Hike at 80% OIS as Yen Nears 160
sections.body:
OIS markets price an 80% probability of a BOJ rate hike on June 16. With the yen near 160, former board member Sakurai called a pause 'unthinkable.' Governor Ueda maintains deliberate ambiguity, leaving forward guidance tone as the primary market variable.

With the hike priced, the positioning question shifts to communication risk. Dovish guidance supports equities; hawkish guidance pressures property and domestic consumption names. Watch press conference language on 'gradual' versus 'data-dependent' phrasing as the real signal.
sections.takeaway: The hike is priced — Ueda's press conference language on subsequent move pace is what moves markets on June 16.
sections.source: Bloomberg Japan · Macro · June 2, 2026

title: Fujitsu Sovereign AI · SoftBank Physical AI Alliance · Record ¥11.7T FX Intervention
audio_label: Fujitsu Sovereign AI · SoftBank Physical AI Alliance
summary: Fujitsu anchors Japan's enterprise AI market with dual Anthropic/OpenAI partnerships and a sovereign deployment stack; SoftBank's Physical AI consortium swells to 30 firms ahead of NEDO designation. The Finance Ministry disclosed a record ¥11.73 trillion FX intervention as USD/JPY retraces to 159 despite the largest monthly yen-defense spend in history.

sections.title: Fujitsu Stakes Dual Frontier: Sovereign AI via Anthropic and OpenAI
sections.body:
Fujitsu (富士通) announced on May 27 dual partnerships with Anthropic and OpenAI, building a multi-AI integration layer with its Kozuchi platform and Takane LLM. The Anthropic partnership enables on-premise Claude deployment within critical-infrastructure environments. Under a 'Customer Zero' strategy, 100,000 group employees use the stack internally before client rollout. Japan AI spending is forecast at 28% CAGR through 2028.

Fujitsu's dual-model alignment positions it as integration partner of record for Japan's Digital Agency (デジタル庁) procurement requiring domestically operated AI — a structural competitive moat.
sections.takeaway: Sovereign stack + Customer Zero creates a durable differentiator for regulated-enterprise and government procurement that pure API resellers cannot replicate.

sections.title: SoftBank Physical AI Alliance Swells to 30 Firms
sections.body:
The Japan AI Foundation Model Development consortium disclosed May 28 that ~30 firms are in due diligence, including Yaskawa Electric (安川電機), Fanuc (ファナック), Asahi Kasei, Daikin, and KDDI. The target: a 1-trillion-parameter model trained on factory-floor sensor data — weight, temperature, spatial coordinates. NEDO public-private designation in June is the critical gate; METI's ¥6.7T subsidy framework supports it.

For investors in Fanuc, Yaskawa, or Kawasaki Robotics, co-investment = a government-backed call option on the next-generation factory automation software layer.
sections.takeaway: NEDO June designation is the binary catalyst — converts 30 corporate bets into a subsidized national infrastructure program.

sections.title: Record ¥11.73T FX Intervention — Yen Retraces to 159
sections.body:
Japan's Finance Ministry disclosed May 29 that authorities spent a record ¥11.73T (~$74B) in FX intervention (為替介入) between April 28–May 27 — first since July 2024, surpassing the prior monthly record of ¥9.79T. USD/JPY temporarily hit ¥155 then retraced to 159.3. BOJ kept policy rate at 0.75%; three dissenters favor 1.00%. Governor Ueda cited Middle East inflation risks but gave no June meeting signal. Finance Minister Katayama issued fresh verbal warnings Friday.

Structural tension: fiscal authorities spending at record scale while monetary policy lags — June 15–16 BOJ meeting is the critical binary.
sections.takeaway: A BOJ hold with no signal at June 15–16 likely tests ¥162–165 and triggers a second record intervention round.

title: Japan AI Alliance Swells to 30 Firms, Rapidus Enters Customer Phase, BOJ Gauge at 2.8%
summary: Japan's physical AI consortium expands from 4 founding members to ~30 companies as materials and logistics giants join the training-data coalition, with NEDO public-private conversion expected this summer. Simultaneously, Rapidus formally opens its customer engagement phase with a general PDK release greenlit for FY2026, while the BOJ's new underlying inflation gauge prints 2.8%—140bp above the official headline—keeping the June 16–17 policy meeting a live event.

sections.title: Japan's Physical AI Coalition Swells to 30 Firms — Materials and Logistics Giants Reframe the Consortium's Industrial Logic
sections.body:
The 日本AIファウンデーションモデル開発 (Nihon AI Faundēshon Moderu Kaihatsu) consortium — Japan AI Foundation Model Development — has attracted investment interest from approximately 30 companies beyond its four founding members, with roughly ten expected to formally commit capital in June. The prospective new investors, reported by Nikkei on May 28, include 旭化成 (Asahi Kasei), the diversified chemicals and advanced-materials group; 安川電機 (Yaskawa Denki), a tier-one industrial-robot and servo-motor manufacturer; 富士通 (Fujitsu); major heavy-industry firms; and large transportation conglomerates.

The strategic logic shifts meaningfully when materials and logistics companies are in the room. The consortium's founders — ソフトバンク (SoftBank), 日本電気 (NEC), ソニーグループ (Sony Group), and 本田技研工業 (Honda) — are targeting フィジカルAI (butsuri AI, physical AI): foundation models designed to perceive environments through sensors and issue commands to robot arms, factory actuators, and autonomous vehicles. US and Chinese models have been trained overwhelmingly on text and image data. Japan's differentiation thesis rests on operational data accumulated on manufacturing floors across the supply chain: 素材 (sozai, materials) properties from Asahi Kasei, motion and torque data from Yaskawa's servo systems, logistics cycle times from transport groups.

The joint venture filed a NEDO application in April 2026; if approved, the venture converts into a formal public-private program around summer 2026 and becomes eligible for up to ¥1 trillion ($6.3B) in five-year support. The model roadmap targets one trillion parameters by 2027, multimodal capability by 2029, and physical-world sensor data integration in the 2030s. Masayoshi Son's team has publicly floated participation reaching 100 companies and organizations.
sections.takeaway: NEDO conversion this summer would transform a corporate JV into a sovereign physical AI infrastructure project — watch for the approval announcement as the key catalyst.

sections.title: Rapidus Enters Customer Phase: NEDO Approves FY2026 Plan Covering PDK General Release and Full Chiplet Pilot Operations
sections.body:
On April 11, 2026, ラピダス (Rapidus) announced that Japan's NEDO has approved its fiscal year 2026 plan and budget for two commissioned 2nm semiconductor programs: front-end wafer processing under the Japan-U.S. collaboration framework with IBM, and back-end chiplet packaging via the newly operational Rapidus Chiplet Solutions (RCS) facility at 北海道千歳市 (Hokkaido Chitose-shi). The approval locks in FY2026 funding and formalizes the milestones Rapidus must deliver this fiscal year to remain on the 2027 mass-production timeline.

The front-end mandate centers on releasing a generally available プロセス設計キット (purosesu sekkei kitto, PDK) to customers, a step beyond the pre-release PDK shared with early adopters in FY2025. Without a stable, production-grade PDK, fabless chip designers cannot commit the engineering resources required to tape out on a new process node — so this is effectively Rapidus's commercial activation event. In FY2025, the company verified Japan's first 2nm ゲートオールアラウンド (GAA, gate-all-around) transistor operation on 300mm wafers at its IIM-1 plant in Chitose. FY2026 pivots from proof-of-concept to yield ramp and process stability.

The back-end story may ultimately matter as much as the wafer line. RCS prototyped an organic insulating film RDL interposer on a 600mm square panel in FY2025 — an industry first by panel dimension — and will now enter full-scale pilot operations to verify 2.xD and 3D packaging manufacturing processes. チップレット (chippuretto, chiplet) packaging is the architecture of choice for advanced AI accelerators. CEO 小池淳義 (Koike Atsuyoshi) stated plainly: 'steadily progressing toward the start of mass production targeted for 2027.'
sections.takeaway: PDK general release to customers in FY2026 is the commercial activation milestone — it marks the transition from R&D proof-of-concept to an actual foundry business with customer design pipelines.

vocab.ja: ゲートオールアラウンド

sections.title: BOJ's New Underlying Inflation Gauge Hits 2.8% — A 140bp Divergence From Headline CPI Keeps June Meeting Genuinely Live
sections.body:
On May 26, the 日本銀行 (Nihon Ginkō, Bank of Japan) released its newest underlying inflation gauge showing Japan's コア物価 (koa bukka, core prices) — defined as CPI excluding institutional one-off factors such as education subsidies and energy-related government support programs — rose 2.8% year-over-year in April, up from 2.5% in March. This new index sits meaningfully above the BOJ's 2% price-stability target and accelerated on a month-over-month basis for the second consecutive reading. It stands in stark contrast to Japan's official core CPI for April, which printed at just 1.4% — the lowest reading since March 2022.

The 140 basis-point divergence between the two measures is the deliberate analytical purpose of the new gauge. The standard core CPI is artificially compressed by ongoing government subsidy programs. The BOJ's new underlying index strips these out to expose what inflation actually looks like absent fiscal intervention: a 2.8% reading means demand-pull and cost-push pressures are running at nearly double the headline. This creates a pointed dilemma heading into the June 16–17 金融政策決定会合 (Kin'yū Seisaku Kettei Kaigō, Monetary Policy Meeting): the official CPI is soft enough to justify holding the policy rate at 0.75%, but the underlying trend argues for resumed 利上げ (riagé, rate hike) normalization.

USD/JPY is trading near ¥159, a level that has previously drawn 財務省 (Zaimushō, Ministry of Finance) commentary on FX intervention. The OECD, in its May 13 economic surveys, projected the BOJ policy rate will reach 2% by end-2027, implying roughly 125 basis points of additional tightening. Deputy Governor 氷見野良三 (Himino Ryōzō) has reaffirmed commitment to further hikes; the question is timing. A hold is priced in for June, but the 2.8% underlying gauge narrows the bar for a hawkish surprise.
sections.takeaway: The 140bp gap between official CPI (1.4%) and the BOJ's new underlying gauge (2.8%) is a time bomb for investors anchored to the headline — subsidy phase-out will eventually close this gap, exposing the true inflation trajectory.

vocab.en: core prices; BOJ underlying inflation gauge

title: Japan's Physical AI Sovereign Bet, METI Boosts Rapidus with ¥631.5B, BOJ Holds at 0.75%
summary: Japan's largest industrial and financial groups deepen their sovereign physical AI consortium backed by ¥1 trillion in NEDO support, while METI approves a fresh ¥631.5B for Rapidus's active 2nm pilot line in Hokkaido, bringing cumulative government support to ¥2.35 trillion. The BOJ holds rates at 0.75% on a split vote but upgrades its CPI forecast to 2.8%, with the OECD projecting a 2% terminal rate by end-2027.

sections.title: Japan Launches Sovereign Physical AI Consortium — SoftBank, NEC, Sony, Honda Bet ¥1 Trillion on Domestic Foundation Model
sections.body:
On April 12, four of Japan's largest industrial groups — SoftBank (ソフトバンク), NEC (日本電気), Sony Group (ソニーグループ), and Honda (本田技研工業) — established a joint venture called Japan AI Foundation Model Development (日本AIファウンデーションモデル開発). Each founding member holds a stake exceeding 10%. Industrial heavyweights Nippon Steel and Kobe Steel, as well as the three megabanks — MUFG, SMBC, and Mizuho — have also taken equity positions.

The strategic logic is focused on physical AI (物理AI, butsuri AI): foundation models designed for real-world control tasks — perceiving environments through sensors and issuing commands to robot arms, factory actuators, and autonomous vehicles. The model targets roughly one trillion parameters and will be trained exclusively on Japanese operational data. SoftBank and NEC will lead model development; Honda will be the first external deployer; Sony's involvement covers robotics and gaming hardware. Preferred Networks (PFN) is participating in R&D.

Japan's NEDO has earmarked approximately ¥1 trillion ($6.3B) over five years beginning in FY2026. METI targets a 30% share of the global physical AI market by 2040 — backed by Japan's existing position controlling ~70% of global industrial robot manufacturing.
sections.takeaway: This is sovereign AI infrastructure backed by Japan's entire industrial establishment, with a built-in physical deployment network that US and EU rivals lack.

vocab.ja: プリファードネットワークス

vocab.en: New Energy & Industrial Technology Development Organization

sections.title: METI Approves Additional ¥631.5B for Rapidus — 2nm Pilot Line Active in Hokkaido, Mass Production Target Holds at FY2027
sections.body:
Japan's METI approved an additional ¥631.5 billion (~$4 billion) for state-backed chipmaker Rapidus (ラピダス), bringing total government R&D support to approximately ¥2.35 trillion since founding in August 2022. The fresh tranche targets IIM-1 in Chitose City, Hokkaido, where engineers are running test wafers through a two-nanometer gate-all-around (GAA) process developed with IBM. METI also announced NEDO will support semiconductor design projects alongside Fujitsu and IBM Japan to build domestic demand.

Working two-nanometer prototypes are being produced, and CEO Atsuyoshi Koike (小池淳義) has maintained the FY2027 mass-production timeline. TSMC and Samsung both entered 2nm volume production in 2025, meaning Rapidus will launch roughly two years behind; but its model is a high-mix, low-volume, fast-turnaround foundry service aimed at customers seeking alternatives to Taiwan concentration risk. Early confirmed clients include Fujitsu and Tenstorrent.

The equity structure now positions the Japanese government as Rapidus's largest single shareholder, holding 11.5% of voting rights plus a golden-share veto. For institutional investors, Rapidus is no longer a venture bet but a strategic infrastructure program.
sections.takeaway: Rapidus has crossed from paper project to functioning pilot line — 2027 mass-production timeline is live, but customer pipeline depth is the make-or-break variable.

vocab.ja: ゲートオールアラウンド

sections.title: BOJ Holds at 0.75% on Split Vote, Lifts CPI Forecast to 2.8% — OECD Projects Terminal Rate of 2% by End-2027
sections.body:
The Bank of Japan (日本銀行) left its policy rate (政策金利, seisaku kinri) unchanged at 0.75% at its April 27-28 meeting, but the decision was fractious: three of nine board members dissented, proposing an immediate increase to 1.0%. The BOJ's core CPI forecast was raised to 2.8% from its prior 1.9% projection — a substantial revision reflecting both imported energy cost pressure and underlying wage-price dynamics. Spring wage negotiations (春闘, shuntō) produced average raises exceeding 5% for the second consecutive year.

BOJ Deputy Governor Ryozo Himino (氷見野良三) signaled the board intends to continue raising the policy rate in accordance with economic and price developments. The OECD's May 13 economic outlook projects the BOJ benchmark reaching 2% by end-2027 — roughly five additional 25-basis-point increments. That trajectory would make JGBs materially more competitive with global fixed income and put further pressure on the yen carry trade.

For equity investors, the rate path has asymmetric read-throughs. Banks — MUFG, SMFG, and Mizuho — benefit from net interest margin expansion at each increment, adding approximately ¥100-150B in annual net interest income per 25bps across the three megabanks. Export-oriented manufacturers face yen appreciation and higher domestic borrowing cost headwinds.
sections.takeaway: The BOJ's 6-3 split vote and 2.8% CPI revision signal the tightening cycle is real — the June 16-17 meeting and May CPI print (due June 20) are the next pivotal data points.

title: NEC–Anthropic Japan Partnership, TSMC Kumamoto 3nm Upgrade, CPI Falls to 1.4%
summary: NEC becomes Anthropic's first Japan-based global partner, deploying Claude across 30,000 engineers in a landmark enterprise AI deal. TSMC locks in $17B to upgrade its Kumamoto plant to 3nm, cementing Kyushu as a high-end semiconductor cluster. Japan's April CPI falls to a four-year low of 1.4%, scrambling the BOJ's rate-hike calculus ahead of June.

sections.title: NEC Becomes Anthropic's First Japan-Based Global Partner, Deploying Claude to 30,000 Engineers
sections.body:
NEC Corporation announced it has become the first Japan-based company to achieve Global Partner status with Anthropic, gaining priority access to Claude models and joint go-to-market rights across enterprise clients. The initial deployment targets NEC's own 30,000-engineer workforce, making it one of the largest enterprise Claude rollouts announced in Asia.

The partnership gives NEC privileged positioning in Japan's fast-moving enterprise AI market, where domestic companies have historically deferred to US platforms for foundation models. NEC's move is significant because it simultaneously supports the Japan AI Foundation Model Development consortium — a direct rival to US AI platforms — while securing commercial access to Claude, illustrating the dual-track hedging strategy common among Japan's leading technology firms.
sections.takeaway: NEC is running both sides of Japan's AI bet — backing the sovereign domestic model JV while locking in Anthropic distribution rights — a hedge that reflects the genuine uncertainty about which stack will win enterprise workloads.

vocab.ja: グローバルパートナー

sections.title: TSMC Upgrades Kumamoto JASM-2 to 3nm, Locking In $17B and Kyushu as a High-End Node Cluster
sections.body:
Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company confirmed it will upgrade its second Kumamoto plant (JASM-2) to produce 3nm-class chips, a significant step up from the 6–12nm nodes planned at its first Kumamoto facility. The total investment commitment for both plants now reaches approximately $17 billion, with the Japanese government covering roughly half through subsidies under the Japan Semiconductor Industry Revitalization program.

The Kyushu semiconductor cluster is now anchored by TSMC at 3nm, Rapidus at 2nm (in Hokkaido), and a supporting ecosystem of materials suppliers including Shin-Etsu Chemical and SUMCO. The 3nm upgrade positions Kumamoto to serve automotive AI chip demand — Toyota, Honda, and Denso are all within the supply chain — without requiring the extreme EUV tooling density of TSMC's Taiwan fabs.
sections.takeaway: TSMC's 3nm commitment in Kumamoto bifurcates Japan's chip strategy into a near-term foreign-anchor approach (TSMC Kyushu) and a long-term sovereign play (Rapidus Hokkaido), with both receiving massive public subsidy.

vocab.en: Kumamoto — city in Kyushu, SW Japan
Kyushu — southernmost of Japan's four main islands

sections.title: Japan April CPI Falls to Four-Year Low at 1.4%, Scrambling BOJ's Rate Path Ahead of June Meeting
sections.body:
Japan's April consumer price index came in at 1.4% year-on-year, its lowest reading since 2022, as government energy subsidies and base effects suppressed headline figures. The print was well below the BOJ's 2.8% inflation forecast and below the 2% target, creating an acute tension with the BOJ's stated intention to continue raising rates.

The disinflation reading dramatically complicates the June 16-17 meeting calculus. Markets had priced approximately 35% odds of a hike to 1.0% following the April 28 meeting's hawkish dissent; post-April CPI, that probability has repriced sharply lower. BOJ watchers note the divergence between government-suppressed headline CPI and underlying services inflation, which remains above 2% — the metric BOJ Governor Ueda has indicated is the more relevant signal for policy normalization.
sections.takeaway: April CPI at 1.4% gives the BOJ political cover to hold in June, but the services inflation divergence means the underlying tightening bias hasn't changed — a hold in June likely extends the uncertainty into September.

vocab.en: consumer price index / CPI (shōhisha bukka shisū)

title: Japan AI Alliance, Rapidus 2nm Pilot Active, BOJ Holds at 0.75%
summary: Japan's four largest tech and industrial firms form a domestic foundation-model venture backed by NEDO's ¥1 trillion AI fund, while Rapidus confirms an active 2nm pilot line in Chitose. The Bank of Japan holds rates at 0.75% with a divided 6-3 vote, raising its inflation forecast sharply.

sections.title: Japan AI Alliance: SoftBank, Sony, NEC, Honda Form Domestic Foundation-Model Venture
sections.body:
Four of Japan's largest technology and industrial conglomerates established a joint venture to develop Japanese-language and physical-AI foundation models domestically. SoftBank, Sony, NEC, and Honda each hold more than 10%, with additional equity from Nippon Steel, Kobe Steel, and the three megabanks. Preferred Networks (PFN) is contributing engineers on a secondment basis.

The venture will apply for NEDO funding from a ¥1 trillion program running FY2026-FY2031. The target is high-performance models on domestic infrastructure and physical AI for factory automation and robotics.
sections.takeaway: The cap table spanning industrials, financials, and tech signals keiretsu-scale commitment; Fanuc and Yaskawa are well-positioned if the physical-AI mandate gains traction.

sections.title: Rapidus Lands ¥267.6B Round, Pilot Line Active in Chitose — 2nm Mass Production Target Holds at 2027
sections.body:
Rapidus closed a ¥267.6 billion financing round: ¥100B from IPA under METI, plus ¥167.6B from 32 private investors including Canon, Fujitsu, NTT, SoftBank, Sony Group, and Fujifilm. The Japanese government took an 11.5% voting stake plus a golden share granting veto power.

IIM-1, Rapidus's first plant in Chitose, Hokkaido, has transitioned from construction to an active pilot line running 2nm gate-all-around test wafers co-developed with IBM and imec. The company is in active discussions with 60+ potential customers. Mass production target remains 2027.
sections.takeaway: Rapidus's small-batch, fast-turnaround proposition targets a segment TSMC's gigafab model ignores; Fujifilm's co-development role is a commercial signal, not symbolic.

sections.title: BOJ Holds at 0.75%, Raises Inflation Forecast to 2.8% — OECD Sees 2% Rate by End-2027
sections.body:
The Bank of Japan held its short-term policy rate at 0.75% at its April 28 meeting, passing 6-3. Three dissenting members pushed for an immediate hike to 1.0%. The BOJ raised its FY2026 core inflation forecast to 2.8% from 1.9%, citing higher crude oil prices tied to the Iran conflict, while cutting FY2026 GDP to 0.5% from 1.0%.

The OECD projects the BOJ policy rate reaching 2.0% by end-2027, advising continued gradual hikes. Governor Ueda maintains a data-dependency posture, leaving the June 16-17 meeting open.
sections.takeaway: The 6-3 vote makes next-hike timing less predictable; export-oriented names with USD revenues provide natural yen hedges.
